title: Building Collision Simulations: An Introduction to Computer Graphics
beats: Shows 250-particle simulation; plan: animation, first simulation, then scaling
Two animations, 15 vs 60 fps: one looks better; animation is frames
One particle in a box: position, velocity, constant acceleration per frame (dt=1/60)
Collision detection as point vs line compare, left edge first
Collision response: assume elastic, infinite-mass wall, so flip velocity sign
Update function in engine: dynamics then detection code
Tunneling shown; two easy fixes (slow particles, more frames) and a hard one
Continuous collision detection: parameterize by t, linear interpolation, solve for tc=0.23
Real CCD is harder; points to books
Two particles: detection easy, response hard; author skips derivation, rusty physics
Scaling up, shown with six particles
All pairs: 5000 tests per frame; 18M tests; laptop sounds, 1h40m render
Broad phase, narrow phase, solve; we already did last two
Sweep and prune: project to axis, intervals, active interval; 15 pairs down to 2
Variance axis note; 100 particles 1h40 to 3 min
Uniform grid with memory vs checks tradeoff; wasted empty cells
kd-tree: median splits alternate axes, termination condition, special case of unsplittable cell
Space partitioning bad when objects span cells; object partitioning with BVH, overlapping boxes tradeoff
Recap: frames, detection, scale; ideas recur in ray tracing

new_moves.what: Turn complexity into human time on own laptop (1h40m to 3 min)

theory: Complexity is made felt by attaching wall-clock numbers to the naive method, and each optimisation is introduced as the fix for the previous one's stated weakness. The chain grid, kd-tree, BVH is a design-tradeoff narrative, not a list.
velocity: Scene builder: render the naive method's cost as a running counter/timer in the simulation, then rerun with each optimisation on the same scene
Voice: every technique closes with 'cost / when it fails' sentence template
Orchestrator: allow 'skip derivation, link source' as an explicit move when a learner model shows low algebra tolerance
Evals: each optimisation scene reuses the same particle configuration
quote: this naive method ... is just an awful algorithm
